episodes.179432: Daytime heating contributed to scattered thunderstorms that developed in the afternoon and evening along a surface boundary.  Aided by dry air aloft, some of the storms reached severe limits.
episodes.179433: Daytime heating contributed to isolated thunderstorms in the afternoon and evening, some of which produced sub-severe wind and some wind damage.
episodes.179454: An unusually hot and humid airmass led to the generation of some afternoon thunderstorms, with a couple reaching severe levels.
episodes.179526: An isolated thunderstorm produced localized gale-force winds over the upper Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.179530: A lightning strike caused a vehicle fire.
episodes.179539: A closed upper low pressure system approached the southern California coast on June 5. This system provided enough moisture and instability for scattered thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon. A few of the thunderstorms produced brief heavy rainfall. One thunderstorm produced hail as large as golf balls near Stallion Springs in Kern County.
episodes.179546: An upper-level low off the coast of California helped funnel in subtropical moisture into the state resulting in the development of widespread showers and storms across central and eastern New Mexico June 5th and 6th. Reports of severe weather and flash flooding stretched from the Rio Grande Valley across portions of eastern NM on June 5th. These reports ranged from a landspout tornado near the Petroglyph National Monument and Nara Visa, NM to flash flooding. Another round of severe weather began in the afternoon of June 6th producing more widespread reports over the same area of the state. Reports ranged from burn scar flash flooding within the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar and Santa Rosa, to large hail over parts of San Miguel County.
episodes.179679: Widely scattered showers and storms developed over central and eastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon of June 6, 2023. The boundary layer was relatively dry, with dewpoints in the 40s to low 50s, and there was only modest shear. However, steep mid-level lapse rates did help to produce some modest CAPE (500 J/kg). A couple of the storms that developed produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.179701: Stationary thunderstorms developed southwest of Chugwater along Chugwater Creek leading to high flows and flash flooding during the afternoon of the 6th.
episodes.179786: Anomalous atmospheric moisture with slow moving thunderstorms triggered a few debris flows in Lemhi County.
episodes.180081: A very moist, easterly surface flow advected 50 to 60 degree dewpoints from the central plains into the Billings Forecast Area. In addition, atmospheric precipitable waters were well over 1.00. Steering winds were light resulting in slow-moving thunderstorms. Although some large hail occurred with a few thunderstorms, the main impact was heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.180196: A low pressure system, stacked vertically from the surface through the upper levels, was located over the Gulf of Maine and the Canadian Maritimes.  An upper level disturbance rotating around this low moved southeastward from Quebec to New England, triggering scattered afternoon thunderstorms in southern New England, a few of which were strong to severe.
episodes.180198: A low pressure system, stacked vertically from the surface through the upper levels, was located over the Gulf of Maine and the Canadian Maritimes. An upper level disturbance rotating around this low moved southeastward from Quebec to New England, triggering scattered afternoon thunderstorms in southern New England, a few of which were strong to severe.
episodes.180267: Showers and thunderstorms produced gusty outflow winds and a brief tornado.
episodes.180288: A frontal passage produced showers and thunderstorms across much of northern Nevada. As a result, gusty outflow winds occurred.
episodes.180322: Isolated and small slow-moving showers developed across northeastern South Dakota along an elongated area of weak low pressure during peak afternoon heating amidst upper 80s and low 90s temperatures. A brief landspout tornado was observed 9 miles north of Rauville around 4:00 pm. No damage was reported.
episodes.180763: A mid-level impulse aloft embedded within another larger-scale trough on the backside of a deep upper low over the Canadian Maritimes approached from the northwest along with a surface cold front. A severe thunderstorm developed and produced large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.180764: A mid-level impulse aloft embedded within another larger-scale trough on the backside of a deep upper low over the Canadian Maritimes approached from the northwest along with a surface cold front. Severe thunderstorm developed and produced large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.180861: Weak frontal boundary moved across the state, generating scattered severe thunderstorms that produced hail and damaging winds.
episodes.180989: An East-West oriented broken line of storms moved south through the CWA in the afternoon and evening hours. As storms passed over the Atlanta Metro, a few storms became strong with isolated strong winds of up to 60 mph, most likely from wet microbursts. A storm just north of Atlanta managed to produce 1 hail .
episodes.181318: Numerous ordinary-type thunderstorms developed across the forecast area from the early afternoon into evening of the 6th. A few storms became briefly severe across north-central Oklahoma, producing reports of large hail.
episodes.181430: Thunderstorms developed across southwest Idaho early Tuesday evening and produced |heavy rain and strong winds across portions of the Lower Treasure Valley, including the city of Boise. Social media, weather spotters, and emergency manager reports indicated flooding of many streets in downtown Boise and the North-End Boise area. Water overwhelmed  storm water drainages and flowed onto sidewalks and lawns. Water up to two feet deep left several vehicles stranded in the downtown area. The Connector, a major commuter route to downtown Boise was flooded, as were some apartments, and several buildings on the Boise State University campus. Rainfall rates over one inch an hour occurred with localized  rainfall totals up to 1.85 inches between 6 PM and 10 PM MDT. ||Blowing dust reducing visibility and high winds formed with a strong outflow boundary near the Nevada border around 5pm MDT. Wind damage was reported from Grandview, ID to downtown Meridian, ID.
episodes.181471: Isolated thunderstorms formed in a conditionally unstable, weakly capped airmass with strong daytime heating. One of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.181511: Several rounds of rain and thunderstorms affected much of Montana during the first half of June. Flash flooding occurred across portions of the region, especially across Fergus County as well as the Rocky Mountains. Fergus County was hit exceptionally hard as several days of occasional heavy rain exasperated area creeks and streams. Casino Creek, located south of Lewistown, was washed out in at least two locations with significant road repairs required. Cottonwood Creek to the west of Casino Creek completely washed out Cotton Creek Road in several areas. Across the Rocky Mountains, easterly flow compressed moisture along the Rocky Mountain Front Range resulting in heavy rainfall and thunderstorms. Several debris flows were reported. Portions of Glacier National Park were temporarily closed due to rock slides and debris flows. The Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest also reported several flooding impacts. Across Meagher and Broadwater Counties, heavy rain affected the Woods Creek and Deep Creek burn scar areas, resulting in flash flooding along Highway 12. Flash flooding also occurred just south of Great Falls along Wilson Butte Road from a rapidly developing thunderstorm that produced 1.37 inches of rain in less than an hour at a NWS employee's home along Wilson Butte Road. A brief tornado also occurred across rural Hill County and was greatly photographed, but no damage was reported.
episodes.181549: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed within the proximity of an upper-level low pressure system off the coast of New England. Hail fell out of many of these storms and ranged from pea size (around 0.25 inches) to as large as ping-pong balls (1.50 inches). In some locations, hail fell long enough to accumulate on ground surfaces.
episodes.181678: Low pressure over Southern California brought significant amounts of atmospheric moisture northward over the mountains, producing showers and thunderstorms with locally heavy rain and small hail. A period of heavy rain from thunderstorms over western Plumas County produced a debris flow over Feather River Canyon. Heavy rain also led to minor street and poor drainage flooding in the Quincy area.
episodes.181743: Thunderstorms produced hail up to quarter size in parts of Arapahoe and Douglas counties.  Also a brief landspout was observed in Weld County.
episodes.181795: As a weak high pressure set up over the western Atlantic Ocean, there was a shift to a low level east-southeasterly flow. This resulted in scattered morning showers and storms near the southeastern Florida coast.
episodes.181798: As a weak high pressure set up over the western Atlantic Ocean, there was a shift to a low level east-southeasterly flow. This resulted in scattered morning showers and storms near the Gulf Coast of southwestern Florida.
episodes.181799: As a weak high pressure set up over the western Atlantic Ocean, there was a shift to a low level east-southeasterly flow. This resulted in scattered morning showers and storms near the southeastern Florida coast. Gusty winds and locally heavy rains were the two main hazards.
episodes.181838: A cold front brought scattered strong to severe thunderstorms to eastern Pennsylvania which brought large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.181982: An upper low was located over southern California with west to southwest flow aloft over the Borderland.  A surface low was located along the Rio Grande Valley which brought southeast surface winds to the El Paso area and provided plenty of wind shear for severe storms to develop around the county.
episodes.182008: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 6th. The strongest storms produced hail up to quarter size, and damaging wind.
episodes.182009: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon of the 6th. The strongest storms produced hail up to penny size.
episodes.182213: Forcing associated with a surface trough inland and a sea breeze circulation closer to the coast within a moderately unstable atmosphere led to severe thunderstorms across southeast South Carolina.
episodes.182389: Thunderstorms brought rain and gusty outflow winds to portions of northern Utah.
episodes.182487: Isolated strong to severe storms developed along a surface convergence axis across north Mississippi during the late afternoon of June 6, 2023. Moderate instability combined with weak shear produced a pulse severe storm with large hail in DeSoto County.
episodes.182725: Thunderstorm winds over 58 mph occurred in the southern highlands.
episodes.182811: The beginning of a very wet month began with flash flooding and a few severe weather reports in early June. There was a closed low pressure located over California bringing Pacific based moisture over southern Colorado.
episodes.182863: Scattered thunderstorms over Florida Bay produced several waterspouts in Florida Bay north of the Middle Florida Keys.  A large area of upper level divergence over the northwestern Caribbean and Straits of Florida enhanced convection across the Florida Keys and south Florida.
episodes.183028: Thunderstorms caused wind damage in northwestern Minnesota.
episodes.183325: A cluster of storms moved south across the Greenville Metro Area during the late afternoon. Isolated damaging wind gusts and some large hail occurred, mainly in the Simpsonville and Five Forks area.
episodes.184608: The combination of afternoon instability as well as increasing mid-level moisture pushing northward on the eastern flank of an upper level low that moved over SoCal and stalled over central-southern California. This upper feature introduced a daily chance of showers and thunderstorms during the first week of June.
